item.title: Trump Administration Threatens to Seize Valuable Harvard Patents
item.description: The Trump administration threatened to assume ownership of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of patents from Harvard University, accusing the Ivy League college of failing to comply with the law on federal research grants.
item.dc:creator: Liam Knox, Hadriana Lowenkron

media:content.media:description: The Widener Library on the Harvard Campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Photographer: Cassandra Klos/Bloomberg

item.title: UK Arrests Hundreds of People in Clampdown on Illegal Delivery Rider Work
item.description: The UK arrested hundreds of people in a clampdown on migrants working illegally as drivers for delivery firms, as part of Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s push to stem the flow of irregular immigration.
item.dc:creator: Joe Mayes

media:content.media:description: A food delivery courier in London. Photographer: Jaimi Joy/Bloomberg

item.title: Greystar Reaches Deal in US Justice Department’s Rental Market Collusion Case
item.description: Greystar Real Estate Partners LLC reached a tentative settlement with the Department of Justice in an antitrust lawsuit accusing the landlord of colluding to increase rents across the US, in part, through widely used industry software.
item.dc:creator: Josh Sisco

media:content.media:description: The US Department of Justice in Washington. Photographer: Al Drago/Bloomberg

item.title: Colombia’s Biggest Cocaine Cartel to Talk Peace With Government
item.description: Colombia’s biggest cocaine cartel will sit down with government negotiators as President Gustavo Petro seeks peace deals with the nation’s illegal armed groups before he leaves office next year.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Bristow

media:content.media:description: Gustavo Petro Photographer: Ferley Ospina/Bloomberg

item.title: Trump Wants UCLA to Pay $1 Billion to Restore Research Funds
item.description: The Trump administration is seeking more than $1 billion from the University of California at Los Angeles in exchange for releasing $584 million in federal research funding that the US froze last week.
item.dc:creator: Liam Knox, Maxwell Adler

media:content.media:description: The UCLA campus in Los Angeles, California. Photographer: Mario Tama/Getty Images

item.title: Trump Announces He’ll Meet With Putin in Alaska Next Friday
item.description: Donald Trump announced that he plans to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin next Friday in Alaska, as the US president looks to broker a ceasefire agreement in hopes of bringing an end to the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

media:content.media:description: US President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin at the APEC Summit in Danang, Vietnam on Nov. 11, 2017. Photographer: JORGE SILVA/AFP

item.title: Eleni Kounalakis Drops Out of California Governor’s Race
item.description: California Lieutenant Governor Eleni Kounalakis has dropped her campaign for governor and will instead run for state treasurer next year.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Clanton

media:content.media:description: Eleni Kounalakis Photographer: Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images

item.title: William Webster, Only Person to Lead Both The FBI and CIA, Dies at 101
item.description: William Webster, the only person to lead both the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Central Intelligence Agency and, very briefly, the first head of the US accounting oversight board, has died. He was 101.
item.dc:creator: Laurence Arnold

media:content.media:description: William Webster following an interview at his office in 2015. Photographer: David Hume Kennerly/Getty Images

item.title: Trump DOJ Asks to Dismiss Harvard Suit Over Foreign Students
item.description: The Trump administration asked a federal judge to throw out Harvard University’s lawsuit over a proposed ban on international students, saying the president has broad authority to issue rules restricting the entry of non-citizens into the country.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch

media:content.media:description: Banners on the Harry Elkins Widener Memorial Library at the Harvard University campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts, US, on Tuesday, May 27, 2025. President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to divert billions in grant dollars away from Harvard University and give those funds to trade schools across the US, escalating his clash with the elite institution.

item.title: DOJ Opens Investigation Into NY AG James Over Trump Suit
item.description: The Department of Justice is investigating New York Attorney General Letitia James over the $454 million civil fraud case she won against President Donald Trump before he was elected.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron, Myles Miller

media:content.media:description: Letitia James, New York's attorney general, during a news conference in New York, US, on Friday, Feb. 16, 2024. Donald Trump and his real estate company suffered a major defeat in New Yorks civil fraud suit over his inflated asset valuations, after a judge barred the former president from running any business in the state for three years and ordered the return of $364 million in illegal profits.

item.title: Trump Is Threatening To Take Over DC. Can He Do It?
item.description: President Donald Trump is threatening to have the federal government take over Washington, DC. However, his powers to take action inside the nation’s capital are limited. He’d need an act of Congress to have complete control.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm

media:content.media:description: Members of the National Guard march towards the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., U.S., on Friday, Jan. 22, 2021. President Biden warned the nation to prepare for its darkest days in the yearlong pandemic, predicting that as many as 100,000 more Americans will die over the next month as he overhauls the federal coronavirus response and presses Congress for more aid. Photographer: Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg

item.title: IRS Commissioner Billy Long to Depart, With Bessent Now Acting Head
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

media:content.media:description: Former Representative Billy Long, a Republican from Missouri and commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) nominee for US President Donald Trump, left, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, April 29, 2025. Ethics filings reveal connections between Long and companies promoting a pandemic-era credit associated with fraud and tribal tax credits the Treasury Department has said is not authorized by law or regulation.

item.title: Trump Reaches Peace Deal to End Armenia, Azerbaijan Fighting
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a joint peace declaration with the leaders of Azerbaijan and Armenia aimed at ending decades of war and reached pacts giving the US exclusive rights to develop a transit route through the South Caucasus.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron

media:content.media:description: Azerbaijan's border guards in Ghizilhajili. Source: STRINGER/AFP/Getty Images

item.title: Trump to Tap Biden Appointee to Lead US Agency Overseeing Natural Gas Exports
item.description: President Donald Trump is preparing to tap David Rosner to be chair of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, which oversees key decisions about natural gas export terminals and power lines.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Naureen S Malik

media:content.media:description: David Rosner, a nominee to serve on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), testifies before the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee on Capitol Hill March 21, 2024. (Francis Chung/POLITICO via AP Images)

item.title: Trump Rattles Latin America by Weighing Using Military Force
item.description: The US under President Donald Trump is crafting a confrontational approach toward Latin America that signals a willingness to use military force against drug cartels, discarding the Biden administration’s preference for carrots over sticks to coax countries into alignment with US interests.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vasquez, Carolina Millan, Matthew Bristow

media:content.media:description: US President Donald Trump walks on the South Lawn of the White House before boarding Marine One in Washington, DC, US, on Friday, Aug. 1, 2025. Trump told officials to fire Erika McEntarfer, the commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, hours after a report showed US job growth cooled sharply over the last three months.

item.title: Trump-Putin Summit Looms Closer But Still Lacks Detail
item.description: This is Washington Edition, the newsletter about money, power and politics in the nation’s capital. Today, economics and politics editor Ben Holland looks at the past week’s progress toward a Trump-Putin summit. Sign up here and follow us at @bpolitics. Email our editors here.
item.dc:creator: Ben Holland

item.title: White House to Clarify Gold Tariffs After Ruling Sparked Chaos
item.description: The Trump administration suggested it would issue a new policy clarifying that imports of gold bars shouldn’t face tariffs, after a US government agency stunned traders by formally ruling that they’d be subject to duties.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Yvonne Yue Li

media:content.media:description: Gold bars at the Italpreziosi SpA precious metals refinery plant arranged in Arezzo, Italy, on Tuesday, May 6, 2025. Gold fell, snapping a two-day advance, as signs of progress on US-China trade talks curbed demand for havens even as military hostilities between India and Pakistan escalated. Photographer: Alessia Pierdomenico/Bloomberg

item.title: Private Equity Is Torn Over Being Lumped In With Crypto in 401(k) Order
item.description: The private equity industry has a novel bedfellow in a White House executive order that will pave the way for American workers’ 401(k) savings to go beyond stocks and bonds.
item.dc:creator: Dawn Lim

media:content.media:description: A Trump hat on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, Aug. 8, 2025. Wall Street is ending the week on a positive note, with stocks rising as traders parsed corporate results.

item.title: Bolsonaro Unlikely to Back Investor Favorite in Brazil Vote
item.description: The odds that Brazil’s Jair Bolsonaro will back Tarcisio de Freitas as a candidate in next year’s presidential election are fading, his allies say, a blow to investors who see the Sao Paulo governor as the ideal challenger to leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Martha Viotti Beck, Daniel Carvalho

media:content.media:description: Jair Bolsonaro, left, with Sao Paulo Governor Tarcisio de Freitas, center, at a 2024 rally.

item.title: Carney Raises Soldiers’ Pay, Moving Canada Closer to NATO Target
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government announced a major pay increase for military members, a move that pushes Canada closer to meeting its NATO defense spending target.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt

media:content.media:description: Mark Carney, Canada’s prime minister.

item.title: WTO Sees Less Severe Global Trade Slowdown Amid US Front-Loading
item.description: The World Trade Organization predicted subdued global merchandise trade this year and next, saying activity remains clouded by President Donald Trump’s tariffs on US imports, while lifting its estimate for 2025.
item.dc:creator: Brendan Murray

media:content.media:description: A tractor trailer near the Port of Baltimore in Baltimore, Maryland, US, on Friday, Aug 1, 2025. A top administration official signaled confidence that President Donald Trump’s trade plans will survive even if the sweeping global tariffs that pushed other countries to the negotiating table are ultimately deemed illegal.

item.title: Tense Trump-Modi Call Helped Unravel Decades of US Policy
item.description: In the weeks after India and Pakistan agreed to a ceasefire in May, officials in New Delhi seethed over Donald Trump’s claims that he brokered an end to a four-day armed conflict.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Anto Antony, Peter Martin, Dan Strumpf

item.title: Germany to Halt Military Supplies to Israel for Gaza Attacks
item.description: Germany said it’s halting deliveries to Israel of military equipment that could be used in operations in the Gaza Strip, drawing a rebuke from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs

media:content.media:description: Palestinians carry aid in northern Gaza in July.

item.title: US Court Ends Contempt Proceeding in Trump Deportations Case
item.description: A federal appeals court threw out a judge’s finding of “probable cause” to hold Trump administration officials in criminal contempt of court for sending accused Venezuelan gang members to an El Salvador prison despite his order to halt the deportations.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

media:content.media:description: In this photo released by the El Salvador Presidency, buses arrive to transfer deported individuals from the US to the Terrorism Containment Center (CECOT) maximum security prison, on March 16, 2025.

item.title: New York Warns of $34 Billion Budget Hole, Biggest Since 2009 Crisis
item.description: New York state’s cumulative three-year budget gap has swelled to $34 billion, rising 25% from Governor Kathy Hochul’s estimate in January as federal funding slows, Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli said.
item.dc:creator: Martin Z Braun, Laura Nahmias

media:content.media:description: The New York State Capitol Building in Albany, New York, U.S., on Wednesday, Aug. 11, 2021. New York Governor Andrew Cuomo announced his resignation on Tuesday, bowing to pressure to leave office or face impeachment in the wake of multiple sexual-harassment allegations.

item.title: Poland’s New President Challenges Premier With Plan to Cut Taxes
item.description: Poland’s new President Karol Nawrocki announced plans to cut taxes for families with children, piling pressure on the country’s bloated budget and setting the stage for another clash with the government.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Moskwa, Maciej Martewicz

media:content.media:description: Karol Nawrocki, Poland's president, during his ceremony of investiture at the Royal Castle in Warsaw, Poland, on Wednesday, Aug. 6, 2025. Nawrocki, the nationalist outsider who scored a shock victory in June’s runoff for president, was inaugurated on Wednesday, setting up a battle with Tusk’s pro-EU administration.

item.title: India’s Modi Invites Russia’s Putin to Visit Amid US Tensions
item.description: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to visit the South Asian nation amid deteriorating relations with the US.
item.dc:creator: Advait Palepu, Sudhi Ranjan Sen

media:content.media:description: Narendra Modi, India's prime minister, right, and Vladimir Putin, Russia's president, approach members of the media as Putin arrives at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, India, on Monday, Dec. 6, 2021. Putin visits New Delhi as billions of dollars of Russian weaponry flow into India that would normally attract U.S. sanctions. Eager to draw India into its efforts to contain China, the U.S. may look away this time.

item.title: Warlords Who Surrender Can Keep 12% of Profits in Colombia Plan
item.description: Colombia’s most powerful drug traffickers, extortionists and kidnappers will be allowed to keep as much as 12% of their criminal profits in exchange for handing in their weapons under a controversial new bill intended to reduce violence.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina

media:content.media:description: A member of the police patrols an area with illegal coca plantations in Tumaco, Colombia, on Wednesday, Feb. 26, 2020. President Ivan Duque said that Colombia will likely be able to resume aerial spraying of illegal crops with herbicide this year once the conditions imposed by the nation's top court are met.

item.title: US and Russia Plan Truce to Cement Putin’s Gains in Ukraine
item.description: Washington and Moscow are aiming to reach a deal to halt the war in Ukraine that would lock in Russia’s occupation of territory seized during its military invasion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini, Alberto Nardelli, Daryna Krasnolutska

media:content.media:description: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in 2016. Photographer: Chris McGrath/Getty Images

item.title: Tariffs Are Starting to Squeeze Profits for Trump-Loving Farmers
item.description: President Donald Trump has repeatedly said he loves farmers. His actions, though, are rippling across the agriculture industry as tariffs raise the cost of everything from tractors to fertilizers and squeeze profits for US growers already contending with low crop prices.
item.dc:creator: Gerson Freitas Jr, Erin Ailworth

media:content.media:description: Trump has asked farmers to give his tariff policies time to play out. Photographer: Rory Doyle/Bloomberg
